attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel renders each signer's full name and postal code, contradicting the agreed limit of first name, last initial and city and the proposal's own description. Once published, cached or scraped, the data cannot be recalled, and the flag rollback does not undo it.

The newsletter/organizer-updates checkbox is pre-ticked, so it is not a valid affirmative GDPR consent for EU signers. The label also bundles 'others' from the organizer, so consent is not specific. This contradicts the stated 'signers can choose' intent, and organizer CSV exports rely on these opt-ins.
The duplicate-signature 409 acts as a membership oracle: anyone can probe whether a given email signed a specific petition, which reveals political participation. No mitigation is described.
attacks.evidence: Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass

attacks.claim: GDPR basics are missing for signer data. There is no lawful basis or Art. 9 condition (petition signing reveals political opinion), no retention period for confirmed signatures, no privacy notice, and no access/erasure/newsletter-withdrawal path. Rollback also says nothing about already-collected data.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: Art. 6/9 basis, retention period for confirmed signatures, privacy notice, data subject rights/erasure and unsubscribe flow

attacks.claim: No transfer mechanism is stated for EU signer emails sent to Postmark, a US processor; a DPA alone is not a transfer basis. Postal-code-based region routing is also an unvalidated proxy for EU residency, with no override or fallback.
attacks.evidence: Confirmation emails go through Postmark; DPA countersigned 2026-09-14 ... eu-central-1 for EU-resolved postal codes, us-east-1 otherwise

attacks.claim: The agreed WCAG 2.1 AA requirement is not met. Errors are shown only as colour changes on invalid fields, the aria-live .form-error region is never populated, no aria-invalid/aria-describedby links fields to messages, and is-invalid is never cleared. The only evidence is an automated axe scan, which cannot show conformance for these conditions.
attacks.evidence:
for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid'); ...

... axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations

attacks.claim: The client script mishandles the response. It reads res.headers.get('Location') after fetch has followed redirects, so the header is typically unavailable and window.location may be set to null, which makes the 'happy path Pass' doubtful. A 409, 5xx or network failure gives no user feedback at all. A 422 with an empty fields array throws.
attacks.evidence: if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location'); ... only `res.status === 422` handled; no 409/5xx/network branch

attacks.claim: The state-changing sign POST has no stated CSRF/origin defense or bot protection. Combined with the lack of any rate limit on signing, a scripted flood can trigger unbounded Postmark confirmation emails (cost and abuse). Unconfirmed rows may also block a victim's email for 7 days.
attacks.evidence: <form class="sign-form" action="/p/{{ petition.slug }}/sign" method="post" novalidate> ... ABSENT: csrf token, rate limit or bot protection on POST /p/{slug}/sign

attacks.claim: The artifact does not state how the organizer CSV export verifies that the caller owns the petition. Rate limiting and audit logging do not replace an access check on a file of names, emails and postal codes.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authorization check on organizer export; only "export is rate-limited and audit-logged."

attacks.claim: The rollback only swaps the sign form and is untested in QA. It does not say whether the Recent signers panel is hidden, what happens to pending confirmation emails and links, or whether the purge job keeps running. The rollout watch also lacks alert owners, paging and a rollback trigger.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip `petitions_signing` off; sign form is replaced by the existing "Follow this petition" button. ABSENT: rollback test result and alerting for sign_submit_error_rate

attacks.claim: The signature write and the Postmark confirmation email are separate side effects with no stated retry, re-send or failure metric. A failed send leaves the signer unconfirmed and eventually purged, and only bounce rate is monitored.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retry or re-send policy for confirmation emails; the only email metric is bounce rate

attacks.claim: Read-path scaling is unproven. The load test covers only 400 writes/s, while 15s polling per open page and a per-view recent_signers query have no index, caching or capacity evidence.
attacks.evidence: Load: 400 signatures/s sustained for 10 min ... polling every 15s, cached at the CDN for 10s ... ABSENT: index on (petition, confirmed, created_at)

attacks.claim: No review establishes whether electronic signatures collected via email double opt-in with name and postal code are legally valid for petitions that organizers will submit to officials in different jurisdictions.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction validity review of electronic petition signatures
